workItem: Replace the browser-owned authentication lifecycle with a backend-first Google OAuth/PKCE session architecture, remove the old client login/MFA/onboarding orchestration from the productive path, preserve server-side identity/entitlement authority, and provide deterministic login/logout/session projection.
workItemDE: Browserseitige Login-Logik vollständig aus dem produktiven Pfad entfernen und eine neue backend-first Google-OAuth/PKCE-Sitzungslogik mit sauberem Login/Logout/Session-Vertrag installieren
projectStage: PVC-02 Controlled Implementation with SEC/FΕ cross-cutting boundaries
priorityReason: Productive post-login freezes persist after repeated client-side remediation; Owner directs a clean backend-first rebuild rather than further patching the browser auth lifecycle.
scopeBoundary: Supabase Auth remains the upstream identity provider; the browser no longer owns Supabase session state or OAuth callback orchestration.
Google OAuth starts and completes through backend endpoints using PKCE; Supabase tokens are stored only in HttpOnly Secure SameSite=Lax backend session cookies.
No access/refresh token is exposed through userSession, localStorage, sessionStorage, URL fragments, or browser JavaScript.
The old LoginStepUpGate/RegistrationCompletionGate/onAuthStateChange login path is removed from the productive composition.
Normal login has no AAL2/MFA gate during this rebuild; existing privileged server AAL2/step-up authorization remains a separate protected boundary unless a later owner decision changes it.
Backend session identity is accepted only after Supabase getUser/refresh verification; subscription tier remains server-authoritative by verified user UUID.
Cookie-based authentication requires the global Origin/CSRF threat model to reject disallowed browser origins for state-changing requests.
No Stripe billing semantics, MFA factor deletion, DNS, provider secrets, or Human/CODEOWNER merge authority is changed.

evidence.priorDiagnostic: PR #1257 merged; despite client AAL2 supersession the page still freezes after login, so the client-owned auth lifecycle is no longer the selected architecture.
evidence.openWriterOverlap: No open PR matched auth/login/session backend rebuild scope at branch creation.
evidence.ownerDirection: Fresh Owner direction explicitly requests removal of the complete existing login logic and installation of a new backend login architecture.
evidence.mainSynchronization: Merged CURRENT_MAIN 163cdcec7b7dc2aa18ad3c8d8846ed0d4bf15dda into the auth rebuild at ff87163322f46c188ccf5b26f8816d40df0370df after confirming zero changed-file overlap across the 7 intervening SEO/current-main files.

acceptanceCriteria: Google login is initiated only through /api/auth/login/google and callback is handled only by /api/auth/callback.
Backend stores Supabase session material in HttpOnly Secure SameSite=Lax cookies and refreshes it server-side.
GET /api/auth/session returns one authoritative user/profile/subscription projection or authenticated=false without hanging the UI.
POST /api/auth/logout clears backend session cookies and the landing/header expose an explicit logout action.
SessionComposition contains no supabase.auth.onAuthStateChange, getSession, MFA, onboarding, localStorage auth persistence, or client OAuth logic.
LoginPage contains no direct Supabase calls, password login, registration, recovery, MFA, or OAuth callback handling.
Server identity middleware accepts the verified backend session cookie in addition to any still-supported bearer paths needed for compatibility.
Disallowed browser Origin is rejected server-side so cookie authentication does not reintroduce CSRF via cross-site POSTs.
Focused and full required tests pass on the exact PR head.
releaseCondition: Release on Human/CODEOWNER merge, PR close, supersession, or abandonment; automation has no merge authority.
